column11: AstraZeneca's own Vermont prescriber price disclosure, Truqap short form of 2026-09-30 (astrazeneca-us.com/pharmaceutical-marketer-price-disclosure-vermont.html): Truqap 160 mg tablet at $455.96. The filing states on its face that, as directed by the Vermont Attorney General's Office, the prices shown are Wholesale Acquisition Cost plus 20%, so WAC is 455.96 / 1.20 = $379.97 a tablet. The Truqap prescribing information (DailyMed setid d698c106-2322-401e-b738-cbd83c843ecf, effective 2026-09-28) gives 400 mg orally twice daily for 4 days followed by 3 days off, which the label supplies as two 200 mg tablets twice daily: 4 tablets a day on 4 days in 7, 365 x 4/7 x 4 = 834.3 tablets a year. 834.3 x 379.97 = $317,001. The Vermont form carries only the smallest package size, the 160 mg tablet; CMS Medicare Part D Spending by Drug 2024 gives a blended $349.42 a tablet across the strengths actually dispensed, 5% under the $368.90 WAC the March 2025 Vermont form carried for the 160 mg, which says the strengths are priced close to flat per tablet

the programme is finished and failed. CAPItello-290 (NCT03997123, 923 participants, capivasertib plus paclitaxel as first-line treatment of locally advanced or metastatic triple-negative breast cancer) missed both dual primary endpoints: AstraZeneca's own trial update of 2024 (astrazeneca.com/media-centre/press-releases/2024/update-on-capitello-290-phase-iii-trial.html) states no improvement in overall survival either in the overall population or in the PIK3CA/AKT1/PTEN-altered subgroup, with median overall survival of 17.7 months against 18.0 months on placebo. No filing followed in triple-negative breast cancer
